lines.text: Most people switch on Airplane Mode believing it makes their battery soak up electricity faster.
In reality, the charging circuit doesn't pull a single extra watt. Airplane Mode charges faster because your radio transmitters stop wasting the power.
When cellular signal is weak, your phone's radio power amplifiers ramp up from twenty milliwatts to over two thousand milliwatts just searching for towers.
Plugged into a basic five-watt charger, active cellular pings, Wi-Fi beacons, and Bluetooth scanning burn up to forty percent of incoming electricity.
Even worse, that dissipated radio power produces heat inside the chassis, forcing the battery management chip to throttle incoming current to protect the cell.
Airplane Mode shuts off baseband transmission entirely, channeling one hundred percent of incoming wattage straight into battery chemistry.
On a sixty-five-watt brick the difference is tiny, but on a low-power charger, Airplane Mode isn't a turbo switch: it's plugging a massive leak.
